request.spec:
A rate saved with a from-date on or after the sheet's today is forward-only: it applies only to
claims added after it was saved (by any path), and claims already on the sheet keep using the rates
that applied to them. A rate with no from-date, or with a from-date before the sheet's today when it
is saved, applies to every claim as before. The rates panel, the rate preview and the rate calendar
show the rate in force without regard to this.
request.prompt:

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A rate saved with a from-date on or after the sheet's today is forward-only: it applies only to
claims added after it was saved (by any path), and claims already on the sheet keep using the rates
that applied to them. A rate with no from-date, or with a from-date before the sheet's today when it
is saved, applies to every claim as before. The rates panel, the rate preview and the rate calendar
show the rate in force without regard to this.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've implemented forward-only rates, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**How it works**
- **Saving a rate:** if its from-date is on or after the sheet's today, the store records the highest claim id at that moment. If it has no from-date, or one before today, nothing is recorded and it applies to every claim as before. This works the same for the rates form and the rates import.
- **Working out a claim's rate:** a claim skips any forward-only rate saved after it was added. It falls back to the older version of that grade and from-date that applied to it, and failing that to the rate with the next-earlier from-date. Older versions now keep the forward-only mark too. So if a forward-only save replaces an existing rate for the same grade and date, claims already on the sheet keep the old value.
- **Claim order:** each claim now carries the order it was added in. A cloned sheet keeps the original order, so its rates apply to its claims the same way.
- **Server:** the server's due figures (statements, rollups, settling, period close) use the same rule, in `Rates.java`.
- **Screens:** most dues are worked out in the browser. A new `claimRateOn` in `useRates.ts` applies the same rule, and every place that shows a claim's due now uses it.
- **Unchanged:** the rates panel's "rate today" still shows the rate in force regardless. In the preview, the candidate rate applies to every claim, and each claim's "current" figure is its real due. The test's expected difference (9.00) needs exactly that.
- **No rate calendar:** the app doesn't have one, so there was nothing to change there.

**Data changes:** a new migration, `V82__rate_forward_only.sql`, adds the new columns. It also adds the older rate versions to the as-of view, so viewing a past date still works.

**One change outside the request.** Scenario 1 failed because of existing app behaviour, not the rates work. When today jumped from 03-10 to 03-24, the "day left" snapshot was recorded under 03-10. So viewing the sheet as of 03-20 showed a snapshot the test says shouldn't exist yet. I confirmed with curl that the app did this before my rates changes were involved. I fixed it by recording the snapshot just after the new today is set rather than just before (`today.POST.yml`, `ApplyToday`, `RecordSnapshot`, and a small new `LeftDay`). Audit lines and their order are unchanged. You may want to review this one separately.

I also checked the version fallback by hand with curl: re-saving A from 03-10 as forward-only kept the earlier 20.00 version for the claim already on the sheet. The as-of rates view returns the older versions correctly. That path isn't covered by the tests.
